3. On carefully reading the FIR, it is seen that the entire allegation has been made only as against A1.
This petitioner has been arrayed as an accused only on the ground that A1 seems to be talking to this petitioner over phone.

4. Even if the entire allegations in the FIR is taken as it is, no offence under Section 498A, 323 and 506(i) of IPC has been made out against the petitioner.
5. In a matrimonial dispute, the police will have to be very careful while adding the names of accused persons in the FIR.
If the allegation specifically points out to the commission of certain offense against certain individuals, only their names must be first added in the FIR.

In the course of i n v e s t i g a t i o n , i f a d d i t i o n a l m a t e r i a l s a r e c o l l e c t e d p o i n t i n g o u t t o t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis offence committed by others also, their names can also be added through an alteration report.

Adding the names of everyone without any material, invariably results in filing a quash petition before this Court by the concerned persons who come before this Court with a grievance that their names have been added as an accused without any material or without any allegation or based on some general allegations.
This observation shall be keep in mind by the respondent police.
Adding the name of a person in an FIR results in causing inroads into the liberty of a person guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Therefore, it is a very serious issue when the name of a person is added in an FIR.
6. In the light of the above discussion, the petitioner shall not be construed as an accused in this case for the present.
It is left open to the 1st respondent to proceed further with the investigation and collect all the relevant materials.
If any solid materials are available against the petitioner, she can be added as an accused at a later point of time.
If no materials are available, the final report can be filed as against A1.
This observation will sufficiently take care of the interest of the petitioner.
